title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: streaming stability + function/tool-calls + roles/stop/logprobs + response formatting
author: Aisha Khan
description: Brings Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions closer to parity with OpenAI's behavior. This PR addresses several related gaps: stable streaming semantics for function/tool calls, correctly honoring roles and stop tokens when computing logprobs, and normalizing response formatting to match expected OpenAI shapes. Motivation: customers integrating with OpenAI semantics expect identical event ordering and field names for streaming responses and identical token-level meta (logprobs/stops) for eval comparability. Changes are split across the API compat layer, the streaming runtime glue, and a small SDK shim for Python compatibility tests. Backwards compatible by default: new behavior is gated behind a feature-flag `OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT` that is enabled for the hosted API rollout after rollout validation. Checklist: - [x] Streaming event ordering (system -> assistant -> tool calls -> function outputs) stabilized - [x] Function/tool call metadata included in streaming deltas - [x] Roles and stop-token handling updated for logprobs calculation - [x] Response formatting (content vs message objects) normalized for OpenAI clients - [x] Tests added: unit + integration + e2e streaming harness - [x] Feature flagged behind OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT Related: ENG-4762 (streaming stability), ENG-4768 (function calling parity). Linear tickets are linked and commit messages reference them. See docs/openai_compat.md for rollout notes and migration guide.
